messages:
morgan: Quick repro I built: generator.Stream hangs on Next() when an auth refresh race + http2 stream reuse occurs in our sample middleware. Handler times out, but goroutine sticks around.
talia: Do you have logs showing which goroutine is blocked? Could be the internal read pump not selecting on ctx.Done().
morgan: Yep. pprof shows one goroutine stuck in net/http.(*http2ClientConn).readLoop and another stuck in our user goroutine waiting on iter.Next(). The root cause looks like we swap the token on the request path via middleware by replacing the Request with a clone (we recreate the Request, not the Transport). Some deployments also swap RoundTripper which triggers conn churn.
ash: Two orthogonal problems: 1) sample shows a couple of anti-patterns (recreating transports or requests incorrectly), 2) iterator ergonomics: Next() should respect ctx cancellation immediately.
talia: Suggest API improvements: add NextContext(ctx) to the iterator and a Close() method that cancels internal goroutines. Also export ErrCanceledByContext and ErrIteratorClosed so callers can check.
morgan: I like NextContext. Proposed minimal signature: NextContext(ctx context.Context) bool and Err() returns typed error. That way handlers with deadlines can loop with per-iteration timeouts. Example snippet I used: 
```go
iter := client.Generator.Stream(req.Context(), req)
for iter.NextContext(ctx) {
  token := iter.Token()
  // process
}
if errors.Is(iter.Err(), sdkerrors.ErrCanceledByContext) { /* show timeout banner */ }
```
ash: Also propose we add Iterator.Context() to surface the original stream context so libraries can introspect cancellation cause (not to replace err typing). But be careful exposing internal contexts can be misused.
talia: For sample app fixes: show three patterns: 1) recommended: token-hot-swap RoundTripper (token read func / atomic.Value), 2) if middleware must mutate Request, do it without replacing Transport, and 3) defensive: call iter.Close() on handler exit. Add a short snippet that wires Close into a defer in HTTP handler.
morgan: Another SDK helper idea: IsRetryableStreamError(err) bool and IsAuthRotationError(err) bool. This avoids users parsing strings. We can implement by mapping transport/grpc errors to typed error values.
nash: Implementation detail: on the runtime side we can emit a structured gRPC status with a code and a custom header like x-rdwd-auth-rotated to signal server-initiated auth reset. Then SDK maps that to ErrAuthRotate. For transport resets we map to ErrConnReset.
talia: We'll need a small integration test that simulates server sending auth-rotation status mid-stream and assert that IsRetryableStreamError returns true and that Stream helper optionally retries once. I'll add a test harness change in eng-runtime/tests.
morgan: Filed DEVEX-2150: go-sdk: NextContext + Close + typed iterator errors + IsRetryable helper; updates to onboarding sample (link).
devex-bot: created ticket DEVEX-2150 and linked to devex/ci/stream-iter-regressions :white_check_mark:
ash: Can someone update the generator README with the three sample patterns and a short note about not recreating http.Transport? That seems to be the recurring confusion.
talia: I'll draft the doc PR and add the RoundTripper snippet using atomic.Value token for brevity. Also add a tiny troubleshooting FAQ: "stream ended with rpc error: code = Canceled" -> checklist to check Transport reuse, token swap pattern, and to use iter.Err() typed checks.
morgan: Great. Once PRs land, I'll re-run onboarding smoke tests and see if the repro still hits. If it does, I'll attach the pprof and handshake logs in the ticket. Thanks.
